user_state: Scattered. Distracted. Overwhelmed by the volume of things demanding attention. Can't start because everything feels equally urgent.

arrival.heading: One thing.
arrival.subheading: Not all of it. Just one thing. That is the whole plan.

arrival.heading: Your attention is finite.
arrival.subheading: Today you protect it. One thing at a time.

arrival.heading: The noise is real.
arrival.subheading: You don't have to silence it. You just have to choose through it.

arrival.heading: Everything can wait.
arrival.subheading: Almost everything. Pick the one that cannot.

arrival.heading: You are here.
arrival.subheading: This moment. This task. Nothing else has to exist right now.

arrival.heading: Narrow the field.
arrival.subheading: You can't hold all of it. You were never supposed to.

arrival.heading: Single point.
arrival.subheading: Everything becomes clearer when you stop trying to see all of it at once.

release.heading: What is taking up space?
release.subheading: Name it. Set it down. You can pick it up later.
release.field_placeholder: Name what is competing for your attention right now...

release.heading: The list in your head.
release.subheading: Write one thing down. Watch the rest get quieter.
release.field_placeholder: What keeps pulling you away from what matters...

release.heading: What won't let you start?
release.subheading: Name it. It loses some of its hold when you do.
release.field_placeholder: What are you circling around instead of beginning...

release.heading: The weight of everything.
release.subheading: You don't have to solve it all. Just see it clearly.
release.field_placeholder: What feels too large to approach right now...

release.heading: Write down the noise.
release.subheading: It belongs on paper. Not in your head while you work.

release.heading: What needs to leave your mind?
release.subheading: Set it here so it stops interrupting.
release.field_placeholder: What are you holding that is not actually your job right now...

release.heading: Competing voices.
release.subheading: None of them are the work. Name them, then step past.
release.field_placeholder: What is demanding your attention that is not actually urgent...

breath.heading: Breathe once, deliberately.
breath.instruction: Inhale for four counts. Hold for two. Exhale for six. Repeat twice. Then begin.

breath.heading: One breath for focus.
breath.instruction: Slow exhale. Longer than the inhale. Let the body settle before the mind follows.

breath.heading: Ground yourself here.
breath.instruction: Breathe in until the chest is full. Exhale slowly. Feel both feet on the floor.

breath.heading: The breath before starting.
breath.instruction: Three slow breaths. Each a little longer than the last. Then begin the one thing.

breath.heading: Reset.
breath.instruction: In through the nose, four counts. Out through the mouth, eight. Shoulders drop. Start.

moment.heading: Name your single priority for today.
What gets your full attention right now?
If you finish one thing today, what is it?
What task cannot wait another day?
Pick the one thing. Everything else is secondary.

completion.heading: You held the line.
completion.subheading: Focus is a practice, not a state. Today you practiced.

completion.heading: One thing done.
completion.subheading: That is not small. In a scattered world, it is enough.

completion.heading: You protected your attention.
completion.subheading: That is harder than it sounds. You did it.

completion.heading: You narrowed it.
completion.subheading: And something got done because of that. Notice it.

completion.heading: Present for one thing.
completion.subheading: In a world built to scatter you. Today, you didn't scatter.

completion.heading: You came back to it.
completion.subheading: More than once, probably. That returning is the whole practice.

completion.heading: The single thing.
completion.subheading: You stayed with it. That takes more than people realize.

home_cards.headline: One thing is enough.
home_cards.subheadline: Not all of it. Just this. Just today.

home_cards.headline: Protect your attention.
home_cards.subheadline: It is the only resource that cannot be replaced.

home_cards.headline: Scattered is not broken.
home_cards.subheadline: It means you care about too many things. Start with one.

home_cards.headline: You don't have to do all of it.
home_cards.subheadline: You have to do this. Just this.

home_cards.headline: Narrow is not small.
home_cards.subheadline: It's focused. There's a significant difference.

home_cards.headline: The noise isn't going anywhere.
home_cards.subheadline: You don't have to listen to all of it at once.

home_cards.headline: Your attention is finite.
home_cards.subheadline: That is not a flaw. Spend it on what matters.

home_cards.headline: One clear thing.
home_cards.subheadline: That is the whole plan. That is enough.

home_cards.headline: You can't focus on everything.
home_cards.subheadline: That is not a flaw. It's physics. Choose wisely.

home_cards.headline: The world will still need things from you.
home_cards.subheadline: After you finish this one thing. Not before.

home_cards.headline: Single point of entry.
home_cards.subheadline: Start here. Everything else finds its place later.

home_cards.headline: The task is still waiting.
home_cards.subheadline: It always was. Now you have this moment to start.

home_cards.headline: You've started harder things.
home_cards.subheadline: This is one task. You can hold one task.

actions.content: Write down the one task that matters most today. Just one.
actions.why: When you name it, you commit to it. The rest becomes background.

actions.content: Close every browser tab not related to what you're working on right now.
actions.why: Visual noise is cognitive noise. Clear the screen, clear the approach.

actions.content: Set a timer for 25 minutes. Work on one thing only until it rings.
actions.why: Finite time makes starting easier. Your brain can hold 25 minutes.

actions.content: Turn off all notifications for the next hour.
actions.why: Interruptions cost more than they appear to. Guard this time.

actions.content: Write your task list. Circle the one item that would make today feel complete.
actions.why: Most lists are noise. One circled item is a decision.

actions.content: Clear your desk surface before you begin.
actions.why: The state of your physical space affects the state of your mind.

actions.content: At the top of a blank page, write: 'Today I am working on ___.' Fill it in.
actions.why: Declaration creates direction. Your attention follows where you point it.

actions.content: Identify the smallest possible start on your main task. Do just that.
actions.why: Starting is the hardest part. Making it tiny removes the barrier.

actions.content: Put your phone in another room for one hour.
actions.why: Even the presence of a phone reduces focus. Distance is the intervention.

actions.content: Write a two-sentence description of what you are actually working on today.
actions.why: Vague is hard to start. Specific is possible.

actions.content: Say aloud: 'The one thing I am doing right now is ___.' Then do it.
actions.why: Speaking a commitment activates it differently than only thinking it.

actions.content: Archive or delete three unread emails before starting work.
actions.why: Clearing small things frees mental space for the large one.

actions.content: Write everything competing for your attention. Then close the list.
actions.why: The list moves it out of your head. You can return to it later.

actions.content: Choose one object on your desk. Focus on it for ten seconds. Then begin.
actions.why: A single point of focus trains the attention before you use it.

actions.content: Block a 90-minute window in your calendar for deep work today.
actions.why: Unscheduled focus time gets filled. Protected time gets used.

actions.content: Write the first sentence of the task you have been avoiding.
actions.why: The first sentence breaks the block. What follows is easier.

actions.content: Identify one meeting or task to decline or defer today.
actions.why: Saying no to something creates space for the one thing that matters.

actions.content: Write down three things you will NOT do today. Commit to that boundary.
actions.why: Limits on output protect the single task that deserves your focus.

actions.content: Put on music you work well to. Let it signal the focused state.
actions.why: Repeated rituals cue the brain that focus is coming.

actions.content: Read only the first part of the task description. Then begin.
actions.why: Over-reading is a delay tactic. Enough information to start is enough.

actions.content: Set your phone to Do Not Disturb. Leave it face-down.
actions.why: Passive distraction is still distraction. Remove the invitation.

actions.content: Ask yourself: 'What is the smallest version of this that still matters?' Start there.
actions.why: Scaling down reduces resistance. Progress still accumulates.

actions.content: Rewrite your task in the simplest possible words.
actions.why: Complexity is often procrastination with good vocabulary.

actions.content: Sort your task list by importance, not by urgency. Spend three minutes on this.
actions.why: Urgency feels loud. Importance is what actually moves you forward.

actions.content: Write a note: 'The distraction can wait. This cannot.' Leave it visible.
actions.why: External reminders interrupt the automatic reach toward distraction.

actions.content: Take three slow breaths before opening your inbox.
actions.why: A moment of intention before reactive space changes how you move through it.

actions.content: Commit to working on one thing until the next natural break. Only one.
actions.why: Task-switching costs more than it saves. Single-tasking builds over time.

actions.content: Move to a different chair or location for a focused work session.
actions.why: A change in physical context can interrupt a distracted pattern.

actions.content: Write what 'done' looks like for today's main task. Specific and small.
actions.why: You can't aim at vague. Define the finish line before you run.

actions.content: Before checking any messages, spend five minutes on the one thing.
actions.why: What you do first shapes what you do next. Start with what matters.

reflections.content: What has been pulling your attention away from what actually matters?
What would you finish today if you believed one focused hour was enough?
What is the real task behind the task you keep avoiding?
When did you last feel truly present in your work? What made that possible?
What is on your list that you could remove without real consequence?
What does scatter feel like in your body right now? Where do you hold it?
What would change if you let yourself focus on only one thing today?
What are you using distraction to avoid feeling right now?
How do you know when you are truly focused? What does that actually feel like?
What has been waiting the longest for your full attention?
What keeps interrupting you? Is any of it as urgent as it feels?
What would you say to yourself if you finished just one important thing today?
When everything feels equally urgent, what do you actually want to work on?
What is the cost of staying scattered today? What is the cost of focusing?
If you could only accomplish one thing this week, what would it be?
What does 'done enough' look like for today? Just today.
What has been half-finished the longest? What would it take to complete it?
Is the thing you're avoiding actually hard, or does it just feel that way?
What would it feel like to finish the day having done one important thing?
What part of today's work do you genuinely want to do?
What story are you telling yourself about why you can't start?
When you lose focus, what are you usually thinking about instead?
What would be easier tomorrow if you focused on one thing today?
What does your best work actually require from you?
What would you protect first if your available time were cut in half today?
What has been distracting you that is not actually your responsibility?
When does your focus feel natural? What conditions create that?
What are you afraid will happen if you focus fully on this one thing?
What does the noise in your head sound like right now? Can you name it?
What would you stop doing if you gave yourself permission to do less?

evening_reflections.content: What did you actually focus on today, and was it worth your attention?
What pulled you away most today? Does it matter as much as it felt?
Did you finish the one thing? If not, what got in the way?
What would tomorrow look like if you protected one hour for the task that matters?
What did you learn about your own attention today?
What did focused feel like, even briefly, today?
What would you do differently with your attention tomorrow?
Was what you worried about today actually as urgent as it felt?
What are you leaving unfinished that deserves your attention tomorrow?
Where did your focus feel effortless today? Where did it feel like a fight?
What distracted you most today, and how much of it was within your control?
What did you protect your attention from today? What do you wish you had?
If you had one more clear hour, what would you use it for?
What is one thing from today's work you are glad you did?
